WikiDoc does not endorse the use of any medication or device in a manner inconsistent with its labeling. 6. For the full disclaimer, please refer to the provided link. Overview 7. Sandbox gc4 is an adenosine nucleotide prodrug authorized by the FDA under Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for treating suspected or laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infections in adults and pediatric patients hospitalized with severe disease. 8. Common adverse reactions include nausea, constipation, fever (pyrexia), acute respiratory failure, anemia (decreased hemoglobin), acute kidney injury (e.g., decreased eGFR, reduced creatinine clearance, or increased creatinine), hyperglycemia (elevated blood glucose), and increased transaminases. Adult Indications and Dosage Indications and Dosage (Adult) 9. Remdesivir is authorized under an EUA for treating hospitalized patients with suspected or laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and severe disease. 10. Severe disease is defined as oxygen saturation (SpO2) ≤ 94% on room air, requiring supplemental oxygen, mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). 11. Remdesivir is only authorized for hospitalized adult and pediatric patients for whom intravenous (IV) administration is clinically appropriate. Dosage 12. The recommended dosage for adults is a single loading dose of 200 mg of remdesivir on Day 1, followed by daily maintenance doses of 100 mg from Day 2 via IV infusion. 13. For patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and/or ECMO, the total treatment duration is 10 days. 14. For patients not requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and/or ECMO, the total treatment duration is 5 days. 15. If clinical improvement is not observed, treatment may be extended for up to 5 additional days, for a total of 10 days. 16. Administer remdesivir via IV infusion in a total volume of up to 250 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride over 30 to 120 minutes. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adult) 17. Limited information is available regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of Sandbox gc4 in adult patients. Pediatric Indications and Dosage Indications and Dosage (Pediatric) 18. Remdesivir is authorized under an EUA for treating hospitalized pediatric patients with suspected or laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and severe disease. 19. Severe disease in pediatric patients is defined similarly to adults, with oxygen saturation (SpO2) ≤ 94% on room air, requiring supplemental oxygen, mechanical ventilation, or ECMO. 20. Remdesivir is only authorized for hospitalized pediatric patients for whom IV administration is clinically appropriate. Dosage 21. For pediatric patients weighing 3.5 kg to less than 40 kg, the dose should be calculated based on the patient’s weight in mg/kg. 22. Pediatric patients weighing 3.5 kg to less than 40 kg should use remdesivir for injection, 100 mg lyophilized powder only. 23. Do not use remdesivir injection, 100 mg/20 mL (5 mg/mL), for pediatric patients weighing 3.5 kg to less than 40 kg due to the higher amount of sulfobutylether-β-cyclodextrin sodium salt (SBECD) and resulting higher tonicity of the solution concentrate compared to the lyophilized formulation. 24. For pediatric patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and/or ECMO, the total treatment duration is 10 days. 25. For pediatric patients not requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and/or ECMO, the total treatment duration is 5 days. 26. If clinical improvement is not observed, treatment may be extended for up to 5 additional days, for a total of 10 days. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Pediatric) 27. Limited information is available regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of Sandbox gc4 in pediatric patients. Contraindications 28. Remdesivir is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any ingredient of remdesivir. Warnings Hypersensitivity Including Infusion-Related and Anaphylactic Reactions 29. Hypersensitivity reactions, including infusion-related and anaphylactic reactions, have been observed during and following remdesivir administration. 30. Signs and symptoms may include hypotension, tachycardia, bradycardia, dyspnea, wheezing, angioedema, rash, nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis, and shivering. 31. Slower infusion rates, with a maximum infusion time of up to 120 minutes, may help prevent these reactions. 32. If clinically significant hypersensitivity reactions occur, immediately discontinue remdesivir and initiate appropriate treatment. Increased Risk of Transaminase Elevations 33. Transaminase elevations have been observed in healthy volunteers receiving remdesivir and in patients with COVID-19 during clinical trials. 34. Hepatic laboratory testing should be performed in all patients prior to starting remdesivir and daily while receiving remdesivir. 35. Remdesivir should not be initiated in patients with ALT ≥ 5 times the upper limit of normal at baseline. 36. Discontinue remdesivir in patients who develop ALT ≥ 5 times the upper limit of normal during treatment or ALT elevation accompanied by signs of liver inflammation or increasing conjugated bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, or INR. Risk of Reduced Antiviral Activity When Coadministered with Chloroquine or Hydroxychloroquine 37. Coadministration of remdesivir with chloroquine phosphate or hydroxychloroquine sulfate is not recommended due to in vitro data showing an antagonistic effect on remdesivir’s intracellular metabolic activation and antiviral activity. Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience 38. In clinical trials, graded elevations in ALT and AST were observed with remdesivir administration. 39. Serious adverse events (SAEs) and Grade ≥ 3 non-serious adverse events were reported in hospitalized patients with COVID-19 treated with remdesivir. 40. The most common SAEs included respiratory failure, nausea, acute respiratory failure, ALT increase, and constipation. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy 41. Remdesivir should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the mother and fetus. 42. Nursing Mothers 43. There is no information on the presence of remdesivir in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or its effects on milk production. 44. In animal studies, remdesivir and its metabolites were detected in the plasma of nursing pups, likely due to its presence in milk. Pediatric Use 45. The safety, effectiveness, or pharmacokinetics of remdesivir for treating COVID-19 have not been assessed in pediatric patients. Renal Impairment 46. Remdesivir is not recommended in adults and pediatric patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min or in full-term neonates with serum creatinine ≥ 1 mg/dL unless the potential benefit outweighs the potential risk. Hepatic Impairment 47. The pharmacokinetics of remdesivir have not been evaluated in patients with hepatic impairment. 48. Hepatic laboratory testing should be performed prior to and daily during remdesivir treatment. Administration and Monitoring 49. Remdesivir should be administered via IV infusion only. 50. Do not administer as an intramuscular (IM) injection. 51. Aseptic technique must be used during preparation of the final parenteral solution. 52. The prepared diluted solution should not be administered simultaneously with any other IV medication.
